transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

It is understandable to be concerned about heat coming from your appliance, but in most cases, this is not a fire risk. What you are experiencing is likely normal operation for modern refrigerators and freezers. Here’s why:

### Why the Sides Get Warm
1.  Condenser Coils Location: In many newer fridge-freezer models (especially built-in or integrated units), the condenser coils—which release heat from inside the appliance—are located on the sides of the unit rather than at the back or bottom. As the compressor works to cool the interior, it transfers that heat out through these side panels.
2.  Normal Operating Temperature: The sides can become quite warm (sometimes up to 40–50°C / 104–122°F) during normal operation, especially in warmer rooms or if the fridge is working hard after being loaded with new items. This is by design and helps maintain energy efficiency.

### Is It a Fire Risk?
Generally, no. Modern appliances are designed to operate safely at these temperatures. However, you should take precautions because excessive heat buildup can reduce efficiency or potentially damage the appliance over time.

### Important Safety Checks for an Alcove Installation
Since your fridge is in an alcove between two units, proper ventilation is critical. Here’s what to check:

1.  Follow Manufacturer Guidelines: Check your user manual for specific clearance requirements. Most built-in fridges require:
• Side clearances: Often just a few millimeters to 2 cm (check your model).
• Top and rear clearances: Usually more critical for airflow.
• Bottom ventilation: Many models need air intake at the bottom.

2.  Ensure Adequate Airflow:
• Make sure there are no obstructions blocking the top, bottom, or sides of the alcove.
• If your fridge has a front grille or vent at the base, ensure it’s not covered by flooring, rugs, or cabinetry.

3.  Check for Abnormal Heat:
• Normal: Warm to hot on the sides, especially near the top corners or along the edges.
• Abnormal/Concerning:
• The front door seal is melting or deforming.
• You smell burning plastic or ozone.
• The heat is concentrated in one small spot rather than spread across the side panels.
• The compressor is running constantly without cycling off (this could indicate a fault).

4.  Ambient Temperature: If your kitchen is very warm, the fridge will work harder and sides may feel hotter. Ensure the room isn’t excessively hot.

### When to Call a Professional
Contact the manufacturer or a qualified appliance technician if:
• The heat feels dangerously hot (too hot to keep your hand on for more than a few seconds).
• You notice any discoloration, scorching, or melting of nearby materials.
• The fridge is making unusual noises or running continuously.
• Your user manual specifies different clearance requirements that you may have missed.

### Summary
✅ Likely Normal: Warm sides are typical for many modern fridges with side-mounted condensers.
⚠️ Check Ventilation: Ensure your alcove installation meets the manufacturer’s clearance and airflow requirements to prevent overheating and ensure efficiency.
🚨 Seek Help If: You smell burning, see melting materials, or the heat is unevenly concentrated in one spot.

When in doubt, consult your user manual or contact the manufacturer’s customer support with your model number for specific guidance.
